items.item_text: resume
cover letter
High school diploma or equivalent experience. (Required)

A Patient Services Representative serves as the first point of contact for patients and clients, providing a welcoming and professional environment. The position manages patient registration, check-in and check-out processes, schedules appointments, verifies insurance information, and maintains accurate patient records. This role also coordinates communication between patients and healthcare providers, handles phone inquiries, and ensures efficient administrative operations. Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and excellent customer service are essential to support a positive patient experience.
Reception, Registration, Billing, and Cashiering - 50%
Promptly acknowledge and greet patients.
Provide HIPAA information.
Verify and update patient demographic information and insurance information.
Create appropriate cases and utilize account flags and folder notes as needed.
Update daily schedule to document appointment status, attended, no-shows and cancellations.
Verify patient contractual relationship, insurance eligibility and co-payment.
Collection of co-payments, including posting payments, providing receipt, and obtaining credit/debit card authorization when necessary.
Obtain financial documentation as required by the insurance carrier.
Explain terms and conditions of services and financial responsibility.
Maintain cashiering policies and procedures.
Prepare and route daily deposit, including balancing funds.
Provide limited or back up billing functions.
Enters charges into appropriate charge entry systems within established standards.
ICD-10 specificity, CPT and HCPCS codes and modifiers.
Consults with providers for clarification of clinical data when encountering conflicting or missing documentation.
Notifies appropriate UHS personnel regarding issues that prevent timely data entry.
May assist with insurance denial resolution, including department recirculating error file, and submitting corrections.
Maintains knowledge of health system and departmental related policies and procedures relating to coding practices as needed for assigned duties.
Supports EAP programs with payments, forms, and communication.
Accepts HOF payments and provides related advocacy and customer service.
Manages EMR activation and related communications.
Telephone Coordination - 10%
Answer multi-line telephone system.
Screen calls to determine nature and urgency of caller's needs.
Determine how best to handle, e.g., take necessary action, refer calls, transfer calls and take messages.
Messages must be complete and accurate and routed according to urgency.
Coordinate all incoming calls to assigned stations with providers and clinical teams.
Adherence to University and department standards for telephone customer service.
Prescreen patients by conducting concise, courteous and informed interviews: obtaining pertinent information to determine appropriateness for scheduling.
May complete pre-registration for scheduling purposes, including verification and updating of patient insurance and demographic information.
Schedule appointments for all visits and procedures with appropriate provider, following designated scheduling criteria.
May be required to determine which materials will be required for each appointment, e.g., medical records, x-rays, etc. instruct patients accordingly.
Monitor provider(s) schedules; as assigned, to maintain optimum appointment availability and efficient daily workflow.
Communicate scheduling issues with providers, clinical team and other staff and coordinate with others to resolve scheduling conflicts or coverage issues.
May provide or assist with template changes and other scheduling maintenance functions.
Coordinate patient discharge by scheduling follow up examinations and/or procedures.
Ensure all paperwork is complete and patients have all required information, provide any other guidance/instruction necessary at the end of the patient visit.
Manage workqueues, pools, and EHR messages and resolve any missing items.
Computer System Operations - 10%
Understanding and operation of computer systems and applications necessary to perform assigned duties.
Maintain knowledge of computer system changes/updates, including required training.
Must provide accuracy of data entered into computer systems, following set protocols.
Manage traffic control technology, including training to use and maintenance of kiosks/tablets and check-in devices.
Follow University and departmental procedures to report and resolve system problems.
Medical Records and Referral Coordination - 10%

Process medical records release requests, including subpoenas, copy, fax, scan and transfer medical records, obtaining required signature(s) on releases, provide information regarding charges to companies or patients.
Must adhere to University policies and procedures, pertinent laws, regulations and guidelines governing medical records administration; confidentiality, privacy and provision to others.
Provide limited or back up referral functions.
Ensure timelines of completing referral requests.
Provide appropriate documentation per departmental policy.
Provide referral/authorization numbers as requested.
Provide information as requested to assist patients with obtaining appointments.
Assist with or fax records required for appointments.
May provide coordination of other services.
May be required to provide instructions regarding patient preparation for upcoming services.
Completes chart mergers in collaboration with UHS-IT.
Other Administrative Support - 10%
Provide other administrative duties as assigned.

May include but not limited to; sort and deliver mail, receive deliveries, send certified mail, maintain business machines by replacing paper and toner, arrange for required maintenance, shred services, or repairs, order office supplies, monitor inventory, manage service request tickets, parking monitoring, lost & found management, and communication related to this role, miscellaneous correspondence, and gather statistical data/surveys.
Must respond quickly and efficiently to students in crisis. Must communicate effectively with students, parents, campus partners and staff in distress.
Familiarity with and willingness to learn ICD-10, CPT and HCPCS coding sufficient to identify services performed; including diagnoses, procedures, and supplies.
Familiarity with pertinent laws, regulations, and guidelines governing medical records; confidentiality, privacy, and provision to others, including HIPAA.

Interpersonal skills to establish and maintain effective working relationships with all co-workers; to consistently interact with patients and other members of the public with patience, courtesy and professionalism, both in person and on the telephone; and to effectively respond to individuals who may be angry or upset.
Ability to prioritize competing demands and maintain excellent customer service in a high-volume setting.

Ability to efficiently use computer system applications for all functions required for this position, including electronic mail, spreadsheets, word processing, and medical office management, (i.e. scheduling, template maintenance, maintenance of demographic and insurance information).

Typing skills sufficient to use a computer keyboard for timely and accurate input and production. Writing skills, using proper English grammar, spelling and punctuation, sufficient to compose messages and/or routine correspondence, which is clear, concise and easy to understand.
Bookkeeping skills sufficient to maintain accurate records of patient financial transactions, prepare related financial reports, balance cash box, and prepare deposits.

Organizing skills to establish priorities for own work within stated guidelines; respond flexibly to changes in priorities; and maintain work effectiveness in a setting with a high volume of patient activity and frequent interruptions.
Knowledge of practices and protocols related to medical office procedures, (i.e. medical terminology, appointments, medical records, insurance verification, cashiering, billing, etc.)

Knowledge of health care insurance systems, which may include Medi-Cal, MediCare, HMO, PPO, fee-for-service, county funded coverage, and workers compensation, sufficient to properly obtain and track authorizations, appoint patients, make referrals for consults, diagnostics and ancillary services, complete and submit billing documentation, and explain provisions and requirements to patients.
